memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When the altar was anointed, the leaders brought their offerings for its dedication and presented them before the altar. For the Lord had said to Moses, "Each day one leader is to bring his offering for the dedication of the altar." - Num 7:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God gave a simple instruction for the dedication offerings: one leader each day. Rather than all twelve tribes bringing their gifts at once in a single rushed ceremony, the offerings were spread out over twelve days — one leader, one day, one offering at a time.

There is quiet wisdom in this pattern. God was not in a hurry. Each tribe's gift was given its own day, its own moment, its own honour. Nothing was crammed together or overlooked. Each act of devotion received its due attention.

This teaches us something about how God works and how we can live. Life is often lived best one day at a time. We can become overwhelmed when we try to face everything at once — every task, every worry, every responsibility piled together. But God gives us our days one by one, and He meets us in each one.

Jesus taught us to pray for our daily bread (Matt 6:11), and He told us not to worry about tomorrow, for each day has enough of its own concerns (Matt 6:34). God's mercies are new every morning (Lam 3:23) — fresh supply for each fresh day.

Whatever you are facing, you do not have to carry all of it at once. Take today's portion. Bring today's offering. Trust God for today, and let tomorrow come in its own time.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you try to carry everything at once instead of one day at a time?
- How can you trust God for today's portion?
- What would it mean to receive each day as a gift from Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, teach me to live one day at a time, trusting You for each day's needs. Thank You that Your mercies are new every morning. Amen.
